question: Can my college association use our dues to pay for our end-of-year dinner?
expected_answer: No, college associations are not allowed to use their share of dues for events like end-of-year dinners, socialization, orientation, or excursions. These activities are the responsibility of the faculty and departmental associations.

question: Will the school provide me with a hostel room when I get there?
expected_answer: The university cannot guarantee housing for every student, so most people live in off-campus private hostels. These hostels are monitored by the university to maintain safety, and some offer shuttle services if they are located further away.

question: How long am I allowed to keep a book if I take it out on a standard loan?
expected_answer: You can borrow a book on a standard loan for fourteen days, and you are permitted to renew it for one additional fourteen-day period.

question: Does the student code of conduct apply to me if I'm only doing a distance learning program?
expected_answer: Yes, the term student applies to anyone enrolled in a programme at KNUST, including those pursuing distance learning, part-time, or non-degree courses.

question: What kind of help can I get from the school if I'm a student living with a disability?
expected_answer: Students with disabilities receive assistance with on-campus housing, financial support, and emotional or psychological counseling. The university also works with organizations like the Ghana Federation of Disability Organisations to provide training, internships, and job placement opportunities.

question: Do I have to sign any documents if I'm going to stay in a hall of residence?
expected_answer: Yes, all students residing in halls or hostels are required to sign a one-year housing contract that binds them to the payment of their room fees.

question: What happens if I miss too many lectures without permission?
expected_answer: If you are absent from a course for three or more cumulative lecture periods without permission, you will be compulsorily deferred.

question: How far is the KNUST campus from the center of Kumasi?
expected_answer: The main campus is located approximately seven kilometers away from the city's central business district.

question: Where can I go on campus if I need to report a security incident at night?
expected_answer: You can visit the Charge Offices located at either the KSS Headquarters near the College of Art, Built Environment and Education or the Main Office near the University Hospital, as both are open 24 hours a day to receive reports.

question: How do I calculate my cumulative weighted marks and credits at the end of my first year?
expected_answer: You calculate your cumulative weighted marks by adding the total weighted marks from both semesters, and your cumulative credits by adding the total credits earned in both semesters. For example, based on the provided data, you would add 720 and 883 to get 1603 cumulative weighted marks, and 17 plus 17 to get 34 cumulative credits.

question: What happens if there's a conflict between this handbook and another university document?
expected_answer: If there is any disagreement between different handbooks, the rules in this Student Guide and Code of Conduct will take priority.

question: Can I use the school's logo on my personal social media profile?
expected_answer: No, you are not allowed to use the university's logo or name on your personal social media accounts because it creates legal risks for both you and the university.

question: How do I get an academic tutor to help me with my studies?
expected_answer: Every student is assigned an academic tutor at their faculty who is responsible for providing guidance and advice throughout their program. It is your responsibility to make sure you visit your tutor regularly for the support you need.

question: Do I need to pay for my medical treatment at the school hospital when I'm on campus during the holidays?
expected_answer: No, the university does not cover the expenses for your medical care at the KNUST Hospital during vacation periods.

question: Who is actually in charge of running the school and handling discipline?
expected_answer: The Vice-Chancellor serves as the academic and administrative head, as well as the chief disciplinary officer of the university.

question: What happens if I miss too many lectures in a course?
expected_answer: If you miss three or more cumulative lecture periods without permission, you will not be allowed to take the end-of-semester exam for that course and must repeat it later.

question: If someone on campus has AIDS, will I be at risk of catching it just by being their roommate or classmate?
expected_answer: No, you are not at risk because AIDS is not spread through casual social contact or being in the same room as someone. The virus is only transmitted through specific exchanges of bodily fluids, such as through blood transfusions, shared needles, or intimate contact.

question: What do I need to do to register for my courses at the start of a new semester?
expected_answer: Before registering for courses online via the university website or AIM, you must pay all your fees for the semester and complete your biometric registration on campus.

question: What is the main reason why KNUST has a student handbook and code of conduct?
expected_answer: The university created this guide to help maintain a suitable environment for academic success, social growth, and self-discipline for all students.

question: Am I allowed to bring my phone or smart watch into the exam hall?
expected_answer: No, you are not permitted to have any smart devices, including mobile phones and smart watches, in the examination room. If you are caught with these items, an invigilator can confiscate them and report you for breaching examination regulations.

question: If I'm finishing my degree but my CWA is below 45.00, does that mean I won't graduate?
expected_answer: No, you are allowed to use your grace period to raise your CWA to at least 45.00 so that you can qualify for your degree or certificate.

question: What do I need to achieve to be allowed to start my thesis research?
expected_answer: To start your thesis, you must pass all your required courses with at least 50%, maintain a CWA of at least 55.00, and meet any additional requirements set by your department or the School of Graduate Studies.

question: If I am a victim of sexual assault on campus, what kind of help or support can I expect from the university?
expected_answer: The university provides support by assisting you with evidence collection, including medical exams, and by taking steps to prevent further contact from the assailant. Additionally, the university will help you explore options for changing your living or academic arrangements if those changes are available.

question: What happens if I don't finish my disciplinary sanctions on time?
expected_answer: If you fail to complete your sanctions by the deadline, you will be blocked from registering for classes, getting financial aid, receiving your degree, or requesting any transcripts until you comply with all requirements.

question: If I'm being harassed on campus, who should I report it to first?
expected_answer: You should report the incident directly to the Directorate of Student Affairs before trying to seek help anywhere else.

question: What kind of student behaviors are considered really serious offenses by the school?
expected_answer: The university considers acts of academic dishonesty, any disruption to university functions, and actions that threaten the health or safety of others to be grave violations.

question: What are some of the engineering courses I can study as an undergraduate at KNUST?
expected_answer: KNUST offers various undergraduate engineering programs including Aerospace, Agricultural, Automobile, Biomedical, Chemical, Civil, Computer, Electrical/Electronic, Geological, Geomatic, Industrial, and Marine Engineering.

question: When did the school start giving out its own degrees?
expected_answer: The university began awarding its own degrees in June 1964.

question: What kind of help can I get from the school if I'm struggling financially or need guidance with my stay on campus?
expected_answer: The Directorate offers various welfare services including financial support for needy students, advice on finding off-campus housing, and orientation programs to help you settle into the university.

question: Which of the halls on campus is the biggest in terms of student capacity?
expected_answer: Unity Hall is the largest hall at KNUST, currently accommodating approximately 2000 students.

question: What do we need to submit to the school to get our student club officially registered?
expected_answer: To register, you must submit an application letter through your department or patron, a support letter from a Senior Member patron, and a letter from the SRC Secretary confirming your constitution aligns with theirs. You also need to provide proof of registration, a detailed copy of your constitution, a signed member list, and if you are a religious group, approval from the Chaplaincy.

question: I'm really struggling to afford basic needs like food and clothes, is there any help available for me on campus?
expected_answer: Yes, you can visit the Directorate of Student Affairs (DoSA) to access the Food and Clothing Bank, provided you have a recommendation from your College Counsellor.

question: If I've been sexually assaulted but I'm not ready to involve the police yet, can I still get forensic evidence collected?
expected_answer: Yes, you can choose not to contact law enforcement or file a police report and still have forensic evidence collected. You may decide to file a report and cooperate with a criminal investigation at a later time.

question: Am I allowed to bring my own lawyer if I have to face a disciplinary hearing at school?
expected_answer: Yes, you have the option to hire a lawyer to represent you during proceedings, but you or your guardian will be responsible for paying all the associated legal costs.

question: How many members do we need to have to register a new student club on campus?
expected_answer: To qualify for first-time registration, a student group must have a minimum of seven hundred and fifty (750) members, unless it is a JCR, departmental, or faculty-based association.

question: What items should I bring with me to my hostel room, and can I bring my own furniture?
expected_answer: You are encouraged to bring your own bedding, towels, and desk lamps, and you may bring personal furniture like chairs or bookcases as long as they aren't too large or dangerous. However, all original university furniture must stay in the room, and you cannot leave any personal items behind during the summer.

question: What happens if I lose my room key after taking it out of the hall?
expected_answer: If you lose your key, you will get a written warning from the Hall Management, and you will have to pay the cost for the lock to be replaced after using a spare key for three days.

question: What happens if I get caught letting a friend stay in my room without permission?
expected_answer: If you are caught with a 'percher', you and your roommates will each be fined 10% of your residential fees, lose your housing status, and be expelled from the hall.

question: Is it okay for me to secretly record someone on campus with my phone?
expected_answer: No, you are not allowed to record audio or video of anyone on campus without their consent or knowledge if it is likely to cause them distress or injury. This includes taking photos or videos in private areas like restrooms, locker rooms, or gyms, as well as sharing non-consensual explicit images.

question: If I report a case of sexual harassment, is there a deadline for when I have to file the complaint?
expected_answer: No, the University does not set a specific timeframe for reporting cases of sexual misconduct.

question: What grades do I need to have to be eligible to run for a student leadership position?
expected_answer: To hold an elected or appointed student leadership role, you must have a CWA of at least 60 with one trail or a CWA of 55 with no trails.

question: If I get caught cheating during an exam, will they stop me from finishing the paper?
expected_answer: No, you will be allowed to continue writing the paper despite being caught in a breach of the examination regulations. The incident will then be reported and investigated through the formal university procedure.

question: If someone tries to commit suicide in my hostel, who should I tell first?
expected_answer: If you are a witness or roommate, you should first inform your Hall Assistant or Hostel Manager about the incident.

question: What should I do to stay safe when I'm out at a party or social gathering?
expected_answer: You should go with a group of friends, keep an eye on your drinks at all times, and avoid common containers like punch bowls. Additionally, look out for your friends' well-being and trust your instincts if a situation feels wrong.

question: What kind of things are lecturers at KNUST evaluated on by students?
expected_answer: Students evaluate lecturers based on their level of organization, the clarity of their teaching, their ability to create an engaging learning environment, and how well their assignments and tests support the learning process. Additionally, students assess whether the lecturer is respectful, helpful, and overall effective in advancing their understanding of the course.

question: What happens if I finish my final year but I still owe the school some money?
expected_answer: If you have outstanding fee debts at the end of your studies, you will not be allowed to graduate, receive your certificate, or obtain any official documents like transcripts, attestation letters, or recommendation letters.

question: What exactly counts as cyberbullying according to the school rules?
expected_answer: Cyberbullying is defined as intimidating, threatening, or coercing others online through platforms like social media, email, or gaming. It involves posting or sharing negative, false, or private content about someone to cause them humiliation or embarrassment.

question: If I get admission into KNUST, does that automatically mean I'll get a room on campus?
expected_answer: No, being admitted to the university does not guarantee you a place in university accommodation. First-year students are given priority for on-campus housing, but you must still go through the specific online application process.

question: If I've hooked up with someone before or we're currently dating, does that automatically mean I have their consent for sex?
expected_answer: No, having a past sexual history or being in a dating relationship does not automatically mean there is consent. Consent must be clear, voluntary, and ongoing for every specific act, regardless of your past or current relationship status.

question: How can I apply for the university's bursary and what grades do I need to qualify?
expected_answer: To qualify for the KNUST bursary, you must have a minimum CWA of 60. Applications typically open during the second semester, and the bursary is intended to cover tuition fees only.

question: I was suspended for poor grades, how do I go about getting back into the university?
expected_answer: You must appeal to your College Provost for reinstatement or readmission and start the process by visiting the KNUST Counselling Centre. They will help you prepare a self-reflective statement and verify that you have no outstanding financial or disciplinary issues before you can be considered for a conditional return.

question: Do I need to sign up or register anywhere to start using the library's online resources?
expected_answer: No, you don't need to register to use library resources because all students are granted access automatically. However, you might need to show your student ID card if you want to enter the physical library spaces.

question: If I break or damage school property, what is going to happen to me?
expected_answer: If you destroy, deface, or damage university property, you will be surcharged for the loss or damage.

question: Do I really have to fill out those lecturer assessment forms, and what happens if I don't?
expected_answer: Yes, you are required to assess every lecturer for every course you take each semester. If you don't complete these assessments, you will be unable to view your examination results from the previous semester.

question: Can the school block me from getting my transcript or degree if I'm currently facing a disciplinary case?
expected_answer: Yes, the University has the authority to withhold your results, academic transcripts, and even your degree if you are found guilty of an offense or while you are still going through a disciplinary hearing.

question: I'm an international student who should I talk to if I need help with my visa or residence permit?
expected_answer: You should contact the International Programmes Office (IPO). They are responsible for managing the welfare of exchange students and assisting with immigration matters like visa extensions and residence permits.

question: Can I turn one of the rooms in my suite into a study area instead of a bedroom?
expected_answer: Yes, you can convert an adjoining suite room into a study or common area if all residents in the suite agree, you get written approval from the Head of Hall Management, and you return the room to its original layout before moving out.

question: Where can I find a quiet place in the library to study by myself?
expected_answer: You can use the three designated Individual Learning (Red) spaces located on the second floor for Engineering, Science & Technology, the third floor for Health & Allied Sciences, and the fourth floor for Social Sciences, Humanities, Architecture, Art, and Built Environment.

question: Do I need a special sticker to drive my car on campus?
expected_answer: Yes, if you own or use a car on campus, you must have valid documentation and obtain a student car sticker from the Directorate of Student Affairs. Failure to properly mark your vehicle can result in it being clamped.

question: How can the school help me find an internship or a job after I graduate?
expected_answer: The Career Services Centre works with various industries to help students secure internships for hands-on experience and assists alumni in finding jobs that match their field of study.

question: What do I need to do if I want to sign up to retake a paper for a supplementary exam?
expected_answer: You must pay the required fee and formally register for the specific course you intend to write. This payment must be completed no later than two weeks before the supplementary examinations begin.

question: Who can I reach out to on campus if I'm dealing with personal or emotional challenges?
expected_answer: Aside from the KNUST Counselling Centre, you can seek support from the Directorate of Student Affairs, Chaplaincies, KNUST Security Services, the SRC, the University Hospital, or your Hall Tutors and Administrators.

question: What are the rules we need to follow if we want to organize our department's 'Week Celebration'?
expected_answer: To get approval for a Week Celebration or any public event, your group must formally write to the Director of Student Affairs to confirm that you accept and will follow all university guidelines.

question: How do I go about booking a study room for my group in the library?
expected_answer: You can reserve a room for a group of four to ten people for up to two hours by booking it in advance. If no one else has reserved the room after your time is up, you may be able to get an extension.

question: Can I have my boyfriend or girlfriend stay over at my hostel room for the night?
expected_answer: No, having overnight guests of the opposite sex in halls of residence and hostels is strictly prohibited.

question: If I get arrested for a crime outside of school, will the university step in to help me or protect me from the police?
expected_answer: No, the university will not ask for special consideration for you because you are a student and will not shield you from the law. The university does not endorse criminal behavior and will allow the legal process to take its course while also potentially running its own disciplinary proceedings.

question: How do I go about appealing a decision made by the Board?
expected_answer: You must submit a written request for an appeal to the Vice-Chancellor within five business days of receiving your notification letter. Appeals are reviewed based on the original report and your written letter, and will only be considered if there is a procedural error, significant new evidence, or if the sanction is disproportionate to the offense.

question: Can I take a break from my studies for just one semester?
expected_answer: No, you cannot defer your programme for only one semester under any circumstances; the maximum period allowed is one academic year.

question: Do I have to pay anything if I want to talk to someone at the counselling center?
expected_answer: No, all services provided to students by the KNUST Counselling Centre are completely free of charge.

question: What is the purpose of the online lecturer evaluations we do?
expected_answer: The online assessment of lecturers and courses is conducted by QAPO to monitor and improve teaching and learning processes, ensuring they remain efficient and effective.

question: Where can I find the most recent updates to the handbook if it gets changed after printing?
expected_answer: You can find any updates to the Students' Guide and Code of Conduct on the official university website at http://www.knust.edu.gh.

question: Can I have a friend stay over in my hall room for a couple of nights?
expected_answer: Yes, you can have occasional overnight guests, but they must be checked in and out at the Hall Assistants' Office and cannot be of the opposite sex. If a guest stays for more than two consecutive nights, you must get prior approval from your Hall Master or Warden.

question: If I'm feeling sick, where should I go for treatment and at what times?
expected_answer: You should visit the Student Clinic first, which is open from 8 am to 8 pm, Monday through Saturday. If you need care outside of those hours or on Sundays, you should go to the main University Hospital.

question: Will the school tell my parents if I get into trouble for using drugs or alcohol?
expected_answer: Yes, KNUST will notify your parents if you are found responsible for drug-related violations, show a pattern of alcohol or drug abuse, or if the university has concerns regarding your personal safety and well-being.

question: If I experience sexual harassment on campus, who can I talk to or report it to?
expected_answer: You can report sexual harassment to administrators, department heads, faculty deans, the Director of Student Affairs, the Head of Counselling, college counsellors, supervisors, the Head of Security, or the Director of Human Resources. If you prefer, you can also contact the Security Department or the Directorate of Student Affairs directly to file a report.

question: If I get into trouble for something that is also against the law, will the university handle it like a regular court case?
expected_answer: No, the university conduct process is informal and separate from criminal law, focusing on educational outcomes rather than legal guilt. If your actions are criminal in nature, the university may refer the matter to the police to be handled through the Ghanaian court system.

question: How can I find a safe place to stay off-campus without getting scammed?
expected_answer: You can use the KNUST Off-campus Students' Accommodation Support System (KOSASS), which helps you find verified hostels, check prices, and interact directly with hostel owners to avoid fraudulent agents.

question: Who is actually in charge of running things at the college level?
expected_answer: The Provost serves as the administrative head of the college, assisted by Deans who lead faculties and Heads of Departments, while the College Registrar manages daily operations with help from other administrative staff.

question: I want to put up some posters for an event on campus, what rules do I need to follow so I don't get in trouble?
expected_answer: You must ensure your organization's name is on the posters, use only tacks or tape that won't damage surfaces, and remove them within 24 hours after the event. Avoid using glue or posting on restricted areas like trees, walls, or windows, and seek approval from the Estate Office if you plan to use banners or exceptionally large signs.

question: Who should I talk to if I want to put up a poster or banner on campus?
expected_answer: You need to contact the University Relations Office (URO), as they are responsible for regulating all notices, posters, and banners placed on campus.

question: What should I do if I notice someone else cheating in my class?
expected_answer: You are responsible for knowing the academic integrity policy and should report any observed violations to your lecturer, department head, dean, or the provost.

question: What happens if I get caught messing with the fire alarms or pull one when there isn't actually a fire?
expected_answer: You could face a GH₵ 200.00 fine for a false alarm, and you may also be subject to further disciplinary or legal action for tampering with fire safety equipment.

question: What are the different degree programs I can study under this college?
expected_answer: The college offers six four-year undergraduate programs leading to a BSc degree: Agribusiness Management, Agricultural Biotechnology, Agriculture, Aquaculture and Water Resource Management, Forest Resources Technology, and Landscape Design and Management.

question: I'm really unhappy with my exam grade and want it re-marked, what do I need to do?
expected_answer: You must submit a formal request to the Vice-Chancellor via your Head of Department, Dean, and Provost within one month of the Academic Board approving your results. You will also need to pay a fee, which is only refundable if your grade improves after the re-marking.

question: How do I calculate my CWA for a semester?
expected_answer: You calculate your CWA by multiplying the credits for each course by the marks obtained to get the weighted marks, then dividing the total weighted marks by the total credits for the semester.
